summary: The subject check and the census compare a form against a statement as a word: a tag inside another word names nothing, while a glued citation number and a spaced-out form still name their entity.
why: Decision 20 made the comparison a substring, and a substring has no word boundary. The run-13 RCA, re-checked by script against the retained captures of runs 11 to 13, found eight of run-12's fifteen projected subjects to be the entity's three-letter tag inside a longer word: RTI in "vertical" and "portion", OCC in "occur", MAR in "mark", OBS in "observations". Run-13's census counts 33 records attachable and 49 ambiguous where a word-bounded rule counts 26 and 43. So one predicate now serves both sites: a form's non-whitespace characters occur in the statement in order, with any whitespace between them, case-folded on both sides, and the characters bounding the match are not letters. A digit bounds a word deliberately, so the text layer's "lithosphere13" still names the lithosphere and "R C 2" still names the record tagged RC2. The cost is the inflected and the glued form: the producer-set subjects of runs 11 to 13 fail three times, run-11's "axial valley" once and run-13's "velocity model" against "velocity models" twice, and the skill sends those forms to tags. The refusal keeps its reason and now says the form must occur as a word. Decision 23 carries the evidence.
